faqs.question: Which night should I host a Diwali party in 2027?
faqs.answer: Saturday 30 October 2027 is the strongest choice: it is a weekend, it falls after Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October, and Drik Panchang lists Govardhan Puja and Dyuta Krida that day. Thursday 28 October suits a small dinner, and Saturday 23 October works for office friends who will be away during the festival.

faqs.question: What theme works for a Diwali party at home?
faqs.answer: A lights theme with a white and gold dress code works for most mixed groups of 15 to 25 people. For adults only, a cards-and-chaat evening suits 8 to 16 guests, and for young children a two-hour lantern and diya painting party is easier to run.

faqs.question: What games can adults and children play together on Diwali?
faqs.answer: Relay and drawing games work across ages because the rules take under 30 seconds to explain. A diya spoon relay, a chalk drawing game with Diwali clues and antakshari all suit a table where a grandparent is paired with a child.

faqs.question: Is it legal to play cards for money at a Diwali party?
faqs.answer: Gambling law in India is made by each state, and most state laws were written to prohibit gambling on physical premises, so a money table at home carries real risk. This page gives no betting rules; play Mendikot, Bluff, Gadha or Sevens for points on a whiteboard instead.

faqs.question: Why do people play cards on Diwali?
faqs.answer: Card and dice play is an old Diwali custom, and Drik Panchang still lists Dyuta Krida, ritual dice play, on Bali Pratipada, which is Saturday 30 October in 2027. A 2024 Indian Journal of Psychiatry editorial describes gambling during Diwali as a long-standing tradition.

faqs.question: How much food do I need for 20 guests?
faqs.answer: As a kitchen rule of thumb, plan about 120 starter pieces, 1.6 kg of raw rice, 1 kg of raw dal, 80 puris and 120 sweet pieces across three kinds. Add about 12 litres of a welcome drink for a four-hour party.

faqs.question: How early should I send Diwali party invitations?
faqs.answer: Send them 14 days ahead, which is Saturday 16 October for a party on 30 October 2027, and chase replies a week before. Expect a late headcount: in SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, no page was made more than 7 days ahead of the festival.

faqs.question: What should I name my Diwali party?
faqs.answer: A short Hinglish name reads well on an invite, such as Roshni Raat (night of light), Mithai Mehfil or Taash, Tikki and Tales. Pick one that tells guests what the night is about, cards, food or lights.

faqs.question: How do I run a Diwali party without firecrackers?
faqs.answer: Hold it in daylight, for example 11 am to 2 pm on Saturday 30 October 2027, and fill the time with games, a shared diya lighting and food. This suits homes with pets, infants or elderly guests.

faqs.question: How can I include a friend who cannot come?
faqs.answer: Send them something made for one person rather than a group photo. SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali page lets them light diyas and see up to six photos in sky lanterns, and it opens in a phone browser with no app.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Party Ideas for 2027: Themes, Games, Food and a Night Plan

The Diwali party ideas that work in 2027 start with the date: Lakshmi Puja falls on Friday 29 October 2027, so the realistic party nights are Thursday 28 October, Saturday 30 October or the weekend before, and a good party needs one theme, four games with written rules, a food plan sized per head and a 7–11 pm run-sheet. Expect replies on phones and late: 48.3% of the 57,456 recorded views of SubhSandesh pages came from a phone, and in our Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, the nearest festival analogue (n = 89), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself. Below: themes and names, six games, no-money card play, food for 20 and a timeline table.

## What makes a Diwali party different from any other house party?

A Diwali party is an evening gathering during the five festival days, which in 2027 run from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October, per the [Drik Panchang 2027 Diwali calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027). It sits around the puja, not in place of it, so guests have their own rituals that week.

The other difference is cards. A 2024 editorial in the [Indian Journal of Psychiatry by Sarkhel](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11633255) describes a long-standing tradition of gambling during Diwali, and Drik Panchang still lists Dyuta Krida, the ritual dice play, on Saturday 30 October 2027.

## Five Diwali party themes, with names for the invite

Each theme sets a guest count, a length and a rough food spend per head. Spend figures are planning estimates for a home-cooked metro menu at October 2026 prices, EST.

- **Roshni Raat (रोशनी रात, Roshni Raat, "night of light")**: the classic evening, 15–25 guests, 4 hours, about ₹400–600 per head EST, white and gold dress code.
- **Taash and Tadka**: adults, card tables and a chaat counter, 8–16 guests, 3 hours, about ₹300–450 per head EST.
- **Lantern Lab**: lantern and diya painting for ages 5–10, 8–12 children, 2 hours.
- **Potluck Mehfil**: each family brings one regional dish and one antakshari song, 20–30 guests.
- **Patakha-Free Brunch**: 11 am to 2 pm on 30 October, for homes with pets, infants or elderly guests.

Five more names follow. All are written for this page:

- Diye Jalao, Dost Bulao (दीये जलाओ, दोस्त बुलाओ, "light the lamps, call the friends")
- Mithai Mehfil
- Chirag Chai Party
- Kartik Ki Raat (कार्तिक की रात, "a night in the month of Kartik")
- Taash, Tikki and Tales

Decoration has its own guide in this series. One rule here: light the game table brighter than the room, since chalk and cards are unreadable by diya light.

## Six Diwali party games, with rules written out

Mixed ages change which games work. In a 2025 study of 11 older-adult and child pairs, [Cès and colleagues in the Scandinavian Journal of Psychology](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12235071) saw more prosocial behaviour in a competitive board game than a cooperative one, though the older players reported real effort. So pair grandparents with children, keep scoring competitive, and keep each rule readable in 30 seconds.

### 1. Diya Spoon Relay

- How it works: carry an unlit clay diya on a steel spoon round a chair 5 metres away and back; a drop restarts the leg.
- Players: two teams of 4–6, ages 6 up.
- Time: 5 minutes a heat, best of three.
- Kit: two unlit diyas, two spoons, two chairs.

### 2. Rangoli Rush

- How it works: one player draws a chalk clue, no letters, and the team has 90 seconds to guess. Clues come from 12 chits: Ayodhya, kaju katli, sky lantern, new ledger.
- Players: teams of 3.
- Time: 20 minutes.
- Kit: chalk, four chart sheets, a phone timer.

### 3. Roshni Antakshari

- How it works: each song begins with the last letter of the previous one, and every third song must contain a word of light, such as diya, roshni, chaand or sitaare. A team stuck for 15 seconds concedes a point.
- Players: two teams, any size.
- Time: 30 minutes.
- Kit: none.

Singing earns its slot when guests are strangers. In [Pearce, Launay and Dunbar's 2015 study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4632513), adults in new singing classes (84 people) bonded faster in the first month than those in craft or writing classes (51), though both were level by month three.

### 4. Who Lit It?

- How it works: each guest writes one childhood Diwali memory on an unsigned chit at the door. The host reads them out, and guessing the writer earns a diya sticker.
- Players: everyone.
- Time: 15 minutes for 20 chits.
- Kit: chits, pens, a bowl, stickers.

### 5. Mithai Mystery

- How it works: a blindfolded player tastes five small pieces and names each sweet; naming its home city earns a bonus.
- Players: 5–10 volunteers.
- Time: 10 minutes.
- Kit: five sweets in small cubes, a dupatta, toothpicks.

### 6. Five Days Quiz

- How it works: ten one-word questions on the festival week, answered on paper, such as the day of Govardhan Puja in 2027 (Saturday 30 October).
- Players: teams of 4.
- Time: 15 minutes.
- Kit: printed questions, pens.

## Card games at a Diwali party, played without money

The card party is part of Diwali culture, and teen patti is the game Sarkhel names. This page still gives no betting rules and recommends a no-money table, for three reasons.

First, the law: Sarkhel notes that gambling laws in India are made by each state, many adopted the Public Gambling Act, 1867 with changes, and most were framed to prohibit gambling in physical premises. Second, a Diwali party seats teenagers, elders and in-laws together. Third, people with gambling problems usually seek help over financial, legal or social consequences, the editorial says, and a host cannot see that from across the room.

None of these needs a stake. Each suits a different table:

- **Mendikot**: four players in two partnerships, won by capturing the tens; good for couples.
- **Bluff**: three to eight players, the fastest way to get a quiet cousin laughing.
- **Gadha (Donkey)**: any number; the last player holding cards is the donkey.
- **Sevens**: build each suit out from the seven, easy for a ten-year-old.

Run it as a league of four tables and 20-minute rounds, where winners move up a table. The top table picks the dinner playlist and gets first pick of the mithai box, and points go on a whiteboard, never on chips.

## A Diwali party food plan for 20 guests

Food should arrive in three waves, so dinner does not stop the games. These are kitchen rules of thumb for 20 adults over four hours, not a study.

- **Welcome drink**: three glasses per guest, about 12 litres of nimbu pani or thandai.
- **Starters, first 90 minutes**: six pieces per guest, 120 in all: paneer tikka, aloo tikki, dhokla.
- **Mains at 9:15 pm**: dal, one sabzi, rice and puri; 80 g raw rice and 50 g raw dal per adult (1.6 kg and 1 kg), four puris each.
- **Sweets**: three kinds, two pieces per guest each: kaju katli, besan ladoo, gulab jamun.

Sweets get their own guide in this series. For a potluck, assign dishes by category, or you will get four boxes of the same barfi.

## A Diwali 2027 party timeline, from choosing the night to the last guest

The festival week decides which night you can fill. This table compares the four candidate evenings using Drik Panchang's 2027 listings for New Delhi.

| Night | Drik Panchang lists | Suits | The catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sat 23 Oct | Six days before Lakshmi Puja | Friends, office groups | Feels early |
| Thu 28 Oct | Naraka Chaturdashi, Tamil Deepavali, Kali Puja | Dinner for 8–12 | Working day; Bengali and Tamil hosts busy |
| Fri 29 Oct | Lakshmi Puja (Diwali) | Family, after 9 pm | Guests at their own puja |
| Sat 30 Oct | Govardhan Puja, Annakut, Dyuta Krida | Full party, 15–25 | Morning Annakut cooking |

Saturday 30 October is the strongest night: a weekend, after the main puja, and the day tied to the card tradition. Drik Panchang puts Tamil Deepavali on 28 October while some holiday calendars list Tamil Nadu on 29 October, so ask Tamil guests which night they keep.

Working back from Saturday 30 October dates every task. Times assume one host and one helper:

| When | Date | Task | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 days before | Sat 16 Oct | Send invites with theme and potluck dish | 30 minutes |
| 7 days before | Sat 23 Oct | Chase replies, fix headcount, print chits | 1 hour |
| 3 days before | Wed 27 Oct | Buy groceries, chalk, two card decks | 2 hours |
| Party day | Sat 30 Oct, 2–6 pm | Cook mains, set game stations | 4 hours |
| Party night | Sat 30 Oct, 7–11 pm | Run the night | 4 hours |

Chase replies early. In Raksha Bandhan 2026, not one of 89 pages was built more than 7 days ahead, so expect the headcount to firm up only in the final 48 hours.

On the night, games go before dinner. Cards come after it:

- 7:00 pm: arrivals, drinks, Who Lit It? chits
- 7:30 pm: everyone lights one diya
- 7:45 pm: Diya Spoon Relay, Rangoli Rush
- 8:30 pm: Roshni Antakshari
- 9:15 pm: dinner
- 10:00 pm: card league; Mithai Mystery for non-players
- 10:45 pm: chit reveal, quiz, send-off by 11 pm

## When a Diwali party is the wrong plan

A party is the wrong plan for the person who cannot come, which is where SubhSandesh fits, with limits. It does not run games, collect RSVPs or plan menus; it is a one-person greeting page, and each SubhSandesh page draws 11.1 views on average.

For a friend in another city, the [interactive Happy Diwali card on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) lets them light a diya at their door, a row of wish diyas and sky lanterns holding up to six photos, and takes about five minutes to make. For someone you miss beyond one evening, an [I miss you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better, because it is about the distance, not the festival.

## Sources

- Sarkhel, Indian Journal of Psychiatry, 17 October 2024.
- Pearce, Launay and Dunbar, Royal Society Open Science, 28 October 2015.
- Cès et al., Scandinavian Journal of Psychology, 31 March 2025.

structuralLimitations: No Diwali or party data exists in facts.md; the first-party lines are platform-wide (phone share, views per page) and Raksha Bandhan 2026 lead time used as a labelled analogue (n = 89).
Theme spend (₹ per head) and food quantities are labelled planning estimates/kitchen rules of thumb, not sourced figures.
The Cès et al. 2025 findings were taken from the abstract; the full text is open on Europe PMC but was not read in full.

Drik Panchang lists Tamil Deepavali on 28 Oct 2027; the BRIEF reports holiday sites listing Tamil Nadu on 29 Oct. This writer did not re-fetch a holiday calendar (DoPT copies at cap); the post states the conflict without picking.

The prompt's claim that Thu 28 / Sat 30 Oct are the likely party nights was checked against Drik Panchang: Thu 28 is Naraka Chaturdashi (also Kali Puja and Tamil Deepavali), Sat 30 is Govardhan Puja/Bali Pratipada/Dyuta Krida. The post adds Sat 23 Oct as the pre-festival weekend option.
Sarkhel 2024 is an editorial, not an empirical study; it is cited for the tradition and the legal framing only.
